digest.component_or_area: tests/interfaces test fixtures and rebar_repo initialization
propositions: Fixture setup consumes 47% of tests/interfaces wall-clock (361.4s setup vs 391.0s call) due to function-scoped rebar_repo running git init and subprocess spawns (306 ms, 58 spawns per test) across 589 test functions.

Consolidating rebar_repo to a session-scoped template with per-test shutil.copytree copies reduces per-test cost from 306 ms to 22.3 ms (13.7x) but requires four fix-ups: rewriting worktree pointers, setting REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR per test, re-randomizing .env-id and .signing-key, and resetting _pending_cache.

Bare git worktree repair is a silent no-op when run on a copy: it validates by path existence of the template (still present), leaving the copy bound to the template's object store and refs, so a write in the copy advances the template's ref invisibly.

The template must be built in an isolated MonkeyPatch context with REBAR_ROOT pinned, XDG_CONFIG_HOME empty, and config cache reset, so that autouse environment from the first requesting test does not contaminate the template.

A tier-wide autouse guard must reject any store whose git worktree list --porcelain paths fall outside its own REBAR_ROOT, and this guard must use worktree list (not --git-common-dir, which is blind to stale gitdir files).

Residual coverage of the build-from-scratch path is preserved by keeping tests/interfaces/store/test_init_idempotent_scratch.py and tests/interfaces/store/test_e4_init.py exempt from the template and building at runtime.
